text_fidelity_a:
LifeStraw Flex Advanced Water Filter with Gravity Bag - Removes Lead, Bacteria, Parasites and Chemicals Blue, 1 gal I live in the Pacific Northwest and love to get out into nature. Often, we'll take along water but end up needing more along the trail. When I was a kid, scooping water out of a stream never made me sick, but now I know better! LifeStraw has been an amazing tool to have on board, even for short day hikes.

It’s a 2-stage filter that provides safe drinking water in any environment. We have built up a small collection of LifeStraw products, some for our hiking trips, and some in our emergency kit.

This new version is a huge step above the standard LifeStraw. While the original LifeStraw filtered out bacteria and parasites, this new LifeStraw Flex multi-use water filter with gravity bag removes bacteria and parasites and also removes microplastics and reduces lead - exceeds the NSF 53 standard - from the National Sanitation Foundation website: Filters are certified to reduce a contaminant with a health effect. Health effects are set in this standard as regulated by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and Health Canada. Both standards 42 and 53 cover adsorption/filtration which is a process that occurs when liquid, gas or dissolved/suspended matter adheres to the surface of, or in the pores of, an adsorbent media. Carbon filters are an example of this type of product.

For backpackers, hikers and campers, this is a perfect way to drink right from natural water sources. It’s super compact and easy to pack and carry along. Travelers can take this to filter drinking water in places that have a questionable water supply.

There are four ways to use this. As a one-gallon gravity filter bag, as a personal straw (drink straight from a water source), attached to plastic water bottles and adapts to hydration bladders in a backpack.

From the packaging and a little research I did, here are some of the statistics:
Filter Weight: 2.0 oz / Gravity Bag & Hose Weight: 5.3 ounces (dry)
Filter size 6.4”x1.5”
Gravity Bag Volume: 1 gallon
Microbiological filter pore size: 0.2 micron
Removes 99.999% of bacteria, parasites & microplastics
Carbon fiber capsule Improves taste, reduces heavy metals including lead, chlorine and organic chemicals like pesticides, herbicides, and VOCs
Exceeds US EPA drinking water standards for bacteria and parasites
Exceeds NSF 42 standard for chlorine reduction and NSF 53 standard for reduction of lead and other heavy metals
The hollow fiber membrane lasts for 500 gallons and the replaceable carbon capsule for 100 26.4 gallons

Kit Includes: One LifeStraw Flex filter with carbon capsule, 1 gallon / 3.7-liter gravity bag w/ quick connect hose, and a backwashing syringe
text_fidelity_b: LifeStraw Flex Advanced Water Filter with Gravity Bag - Removes Lead, Bacteria, Parasites and Chemicals Blue, 1 gal

text_fidelity_a:
Plano 3640 Waterproof Stowaway This is a great way to store 12 sets of polyhedral dice for D&D and similar games. I'm not sure if you strictly-speaking need waterproof storage for that, but while the O-ring may be overkill, the locking clasps and overall durability are a cut above what you usually find on parts organizers. This is never, ever going to come open unexpectedly and spill its precious contents all over the place!

With the dividers installed as shown in my photo, 8 areas hold a set of 7 polyhedral dice perfectly. Five of those will also hold a set of 12 six-sided dice. The four larger areas hold somewhat more; I have 10 d20's in one of them comfortably.

The downside of this approach is that you're certainly not going to sneak up on anyone while carrying one of these full of plastic/resin dice. And if you're into metal dice, or the sort of gemstone dice where each of them costs more than this whole container, then this probably isn't how you want to store them. (But you could probably pad them properly with a bit more work.)

Color of the O-ring seems to vary. I have two black and one blue, but the Plano part number stamped into it is the same for all three.

If you are the sort of person who needs to compactly and securely transport a lot of dice, this is the best way I've found to do it.

Gear Doctors Camping Pads Self Inflating Ultralight Apollo air 4.3-5.2 R Insulated Camping mats 1.5-3.3 in Must Haves Inflatable Foam air Sleep mat self Inflating air Mattress for Camping cot I bought these for my family to be able to go camping and have some additional padding under our sleeping bags, as well as to insulate from the ground temperature. While we haven't had opportunity to camp with them yet, I have tested the product out in the house.

At first, I wasn't sure about the inflation, but being inexperienced with this type of product, I really didn't know what to expect (would it inflate like an air mattress, or would inflation be minimal?). When I first unrolled it, it didn't seem to inflate, even after the 3-5 minutes described in the instructions. Then I realized I unrolled it with the valve closed, and the instructions state to unroll with the valve open. So, I rolled it back, squeezing out what air had entered it, then proceeded to unroll again with the valve open. After several minutes, I came back, put it on the floor and tested it. It had inflated significantly more (don't expect an air mattress), though still remained thin. For me it was fairly comfortable on its own, and with my sleeping bag on top of it, it was more than comfortable enough for camping.

After testing it for comfort on the hard floor in my house, I rolled it back up, and a lot of air came out. It was easy to roll and easily went back into its carry bag, which is a big plus (too many products never fit back in their original packaging).

So, short of knowing how it would do on the ground outside in cold weather, I'd say this product was worth the purchase. It seems to be made of high-quality material, and it provides added comfort for sleeping in a sleeping bag.
text_fidelity_b: Gear Doctors Camping Pads Self Inflating Ultralight Apollo air 4.3-5.2 R Insulated Camping mats 1.5-3.3 in Must Haves Inflatable Foam air Sleep mat self Inflating air Mattress for Camping cot

text_fidelity_a:
Withings ActivitÃ Steel - Activity and Sleep Tracking Watch I had high hopes for this device. I think it's aimed at people who don't want a gadget to play with, but a useful and attractive minimalist activity tracker. It qualifies as attractive and, if all you want to do is count steps, it is useful. Ultimately, I had to quit wearing it because it caused a severe rash on my wrist under one side of the band. I have reached out to Withings and I will update this review when my issue is resolved (or not). At this point I just want to return it for the following reasons:

1. The rash was severe. I've now gone 2 weeks without wearing the watch and it has barely diminished. I'm not allergic to silicone, so I wonder what chemicals are in or on the band.
2. The lack of contrast between the hands and the face result in a watch I can only read in good light. In a dimly lit room it is completely unreadable.
3. A big reason the watch appealed to me is that I can wear it while swimming. It is supposed to log swim time, but it was unreliable to the point of being useless for this purpose.
4. I was intrigued by the sleep tracking, but it has quirks that make me doubt it's usefulness. For example, if I sit on the couch reading or watching TV for an hour before bed, sometimes it logs this as sleep, including deep sleep.

The watch counts from 50% to 20% less steps than my Samsung app. I can't say which is more accurate. I like the idea of an elegant and simple tracker/watch, and this was almost it. Ultimately nothing else matters because I can't wear it. The negatives add up to the point that I'm not interested in resolving the rash problem with a different band.

Update: I reached out to Withings. They responded quickly and seemed genuinely concerned. They dealt with my problem promptly and fairly. I'm upping my review from 2 stars to 3 stars because of the customer service.
text_fidelity_b: Withings ActivitÃ Steel - Activity and Sleep Tracking Watch

text_fidelity_a:
TRX Training Essentials: Flexibility DVD, Workouts to Improve Flexibility I'm very impressed with suspension strap workouts. Doing strength training, instant adjustments to resistance are possible just by adjusting by an inch or two how close you are to the anchor. And almost every strength exercise, whether for arms or legs, also involves the core. Which is amazing.

But the best thing about the straps are for stretching and flexibility. I can get deeper, longer, more supported stretches with these then with any other method I've ever tried. And my friends have called me a stretch fanatic for years.

This DVD gives detailed descriptions of 10 or 12 stretches, with progressions for each one. Their "workout" is about 45 min. long. Or you can use the "exercise library" which gives detailed descriptions of each with their progressions. Watch the exercise library for a much shorter stretch workout or pause with your remote to work an individual stretch longer.

You can probably find most of these stretches on the internet, but I'm glad I got this DVD which I got in a 3 DVD package that included a strength and cardio DVD. The strength is a pretty good workout. Haven't tried the cardio yet.

Notice I haven't mentioned TRX once yet in this review. Although I do own a TRX and like it, you can get VERY similar suspension straps on Amazon for $24.99. I got RopeInaBag and use it for travel because it is much lighter and more compact while still being plenty strong.

Regardless of the brand of straps you use, I highly recommend the stretches in this DVD.
text_fidelity_b: TRX Training Essentials: Flexibility DVD, Workouts to Improve Flexibility

Ozeri 4x3motion Digital Pocket 3D Pedometer with Tri-Axis Technology I've been using this for 3 months primarily for a fitness challenge where I work. There are some positive and negatives:
Pos:
1. It does seem very accurate for walking distances.
2. I love that I can pretty much have it anywhere on me and it will work the same.
2. I like the calories burned and minutes exercised.

Neg:
1. I wish it has some sort of clip for a belt or waste, as a women I often don't have pockets and wearing a lanyard around my neck isn't the most professional look
2. Durability- Granted this was my fault but after one drop on a hardwood floor from about 3 ft, the screen froze on me, luckily removing the battery and putting it back in seemed to fix it
3. I'm not sure if this is due to the fall or the battery dying, but now after 3 months it's clear something is wrong as it seems every few months the screen either freezes or resets itself. If it's the fall I recognize that is my fault, however I would expect something made for use while exercising to be a little more durable. text_fidelity_a:
Wald 582 Folding Rear Bicycle Basket I wanted to attach this to a pakrak rear rack and had problems because of the design of the rack. The vertical supports that attach near the wheel axel are wider than the top of the rack so the hardare provided would not work. Even if the reach had been long enough the hardware was not big enough to go around the tubing of the rack.

i solved the problem with wire ties and that solution seems plenty strong. If its not strong enough Ill use hose clamps.

The clasp is very difficult to use and really should be redesigned. Others have commented on this shortcoming of the design. I had to use vice grips to bend the clasp so it would be workable by hand. That, of course scratched the paint. The paint on the steel wire where the clasp is attached is thick enough to keep the clasp from rotating freely so it was necessary to open and close the clasp many times with pliers to get it working smoothly enough.

I had planned to buy a second one of these for the other side of my rack but now plan to buy a similar product from another manufacturer and will amend this review after I install the second rack.

Oct 1, 2018 I bought a Sunlite basked and installed it today. I consider the Sunlite basket to be a superior product and provided details on my review of that product.
text_fidelity_b: Wald 582 Folding Rear Bicycle Basket

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Double-High Supportrest. I personally wouldn't spend much on an air mattress because no matter how expensive they are, they always have an ephemeral life cycle. It's just the nature of them.

The construction quality feels a bit heavier duty than other mattress in this price range. So far it is holding air well -- I've kept it inflated for 3 and 4 days without having to refill.

It feels as comfortable as any other air mattress I've used -- certainly comfortable enough for guests staying a few days.

While it doesn't come with an air pump, the air pump I have for my car works with it (it has an attachment specifically for inflating air mattresses and rafts). And based on the price, it looks like you save some money by not having a pump come with it.

My one complaint is the design of the valve. It does not have a way to allow air to flow in but not out at the same time -- so if you stop inflating, you have to immediately close it. I've had other air mattresses where the valve could do that.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Double-High Supportrest.

text_fidelity_a:
NACATIN Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board, Upgrade Version 10′ 6″ Paddle Board with Free Premium SUP Accessories & Backpack,10L Dry Bag, Phone Pouch, Shoulder Strap. So far this NACATIN Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board is pretty darn good and we think it’ll turn out to be a great SUP for us. My wife and I have wanted our own SUPs for awhile, but we have no where to store a regular SUP and had considered blow up versions. When I had a chance to get this NACATIN Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board I took it. Unfortunately for us, it’s taken a longer than desired time to get a chance to try them - and due to weather (storms, hurricanes) and my recovery from surgery, we’ve been unable to get onto the water. So at this point we are only able to review based on the specific SUP and it’s kit - I will update when if need be when we get it on the water. In the mean time, this is a nice set up and we think it’s gonna be a great SUP. The kit is excellent, with items such as a dry bag for your pone included. There is a patch kit. Also a carrying bag. The carrying bag is a little... weird. The bag sets high - the actual straps are set low on the bag so the top of the bag is higher - at the head or perhaps above depending on your size. But it works on. My wife wore it for the pictures and said it was comfortable, but that it set “weird,” and she felt she could wear it from the car to wherever we were to launch, comfortably. But, I did have to help her get it on and off due to the placement of the straps.

Pumping the SUP: It took us a bit to figure this process out, but once we had it, it went fine. The instruction book is pretty tiny writing, so we took a picture and adjusted it. We can also keep the instructions with on our phones for when we’re out. The tube was easy to insert - took a few times popping out to get it to stay on - there is a way to adjust the pump as it gets harder to pump and we did use it. My wife pumped for awhile, then I did. It IS a bit tough to do. NOT the actual pumping, but the amount of time and it does get harder - adjust the dial - but we only got as high as the 8 PSI not to the 15 they recommend. As we get back into shape following being off workouts for awhile, we’ll get better at it, but between us - for this test run - we were only able to hit that 8 and we had to give up. It FELT fine at this level, but WOW....! We WILL TRY to get to that 15, but ... WOW! My wife stood on it and it felt great, but she said she sees how the 15 would be “better,” yet... will we ever be able to get that high. There are two blades on the bottom - and you add the fin - they are in a holder to protect them when it’s down.

Deflating was really easy. And it took only minutes. This SUP has you use the pump to help clear out the final air and that worked great. The prong you push in the air hole is really easy to use and my wife was thrilled with it.

Overall we are impressed with this NACATIN Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and look forward to FINALLY being able to use it on the water - when it’s safe. It comes with a break-apart paddle. We have not used it nor put it together, but we did get ourselves another paddle - we think it’s lighter. We’ll keep them both and take both with. It’s a practice we were taught - to have a backup. But right now I can’t speak to how good theirs is. But we are impressed. at this point, we can’t wait to get out there on this NACATIN Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board!
text_fidelity_b: NACATIN Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board, Upgrade Version 10′ 6″ Paddle Board with Free Premium SUP Accessories & Backpack,10L Dry Bag, Phone Pouch, Shoulder Strap.

text_fidelity_a:
Razor E300 Electric Scooter - 9" Air-filled Tires, Up to 15 mph and 10 Miles Range, White/Blue I just put some rubber bands on the throttle so it felt grippier. This thing is the most fun! I am 5'10 and weigh 180. It does have a hard time on hills but on flat land and down hill it can feel pretty fast. If you want to ride around town just choose flattest routes.

Like with a skateboard....once you learn the correct foot positions to ride comfortably, it is easy. I learned I put my feet on very similar as to my skateboards.

Since the throttle is either on or off with no inbetween....it can feel kind of jerky the first few times you ride it until you get used to that. You will learn it fast though....how to let off or turn on. Turning is not very tight radius so practice that if you arent used to riding one.
Prices are wild on these. I got mine last month for 260...the white e300 with the blue front forks. I see they are over 400 now. I think under 275 is a solid price if you want to play or plan to ride it to your local store or other near by places. Scooter laws vary state to state and where I am this is considered a toy and can be ridden on the sidewalks. Which....no one ever uses here anyway. We dont have bike lanes where I live either so I dont know if it would be legal to ride a bike lane in my state.

It is beefy and heavy and feels like a true machine rather than a toy. Mine charges fine, tires hold pressure fine, no issues at all.
I keep it inside because it flat states on the directions of use that extreme temps can effect the battery or even ruin it.
I have used it on street pavement, sidewalks, and fine gravel. I have never run out of charge on a trip but you CAN still kick scoot this old style if you do run out of charge.

I think it is fun, gets me out in the fresh air, saves some gas money.
text_fidelity_b: Razor E300 Electric Scooter - 9" Air-filled Tires, Up to 15 mph and 10 Miles Range, White/Blue

text_fidelity_a:
CORE 6 Person Instant Cabin Tent | Portable Large Pop Up Tent with Easy 60 Second Camp Setup for Family Camping | Included Hanging Organizer for Outdoor Camping Accessories I camp or yurt at least once a month during winter and up to three times a month during warmer weather. Yurts are great during cold & rainy months but in the Pacific NW, a gal has to prepare for rain every weekend no matter what the time of year.

Set the Cabin Tent up for a trial run in the garage this weekend. I am in my early 40's and stand a towering 5'0". I was tickled to have it setup within minutes, first time. Putting the rain fly on was a bit trickier due to my height but manageable.

Interior of the Core 6 is spacious. Easily enough room for a full sized air mattress, table and gear

Breaking the Core 6 down was a snap.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
09/13/17 Update

I have used the CORE 6 many, many times since my initial review. It has held up very, very well in PNW rain. I do wish the rain fly either extended down or out a bit more as I am not able to open the windows during a down pour without water dripping in them. Aside from that the tent itself has kept the rain out beautifully.

There is A LOT of airflow in this tent and I have tried multiple ways of covering the ceiling netting before attaching the rain fly in hopes of trapping some heat inside. A blanket over the roof (and under the rain fly) kept the heat in very well but it got rather humid.

The bottom of the door can be a bugger to zip up. I have found that making sure the tent is not staked out too tautly in front helps but it does not alleviate the issue. Two hands are definitely needed to zip around the bottom corner of the door.

The Man borrowed the tent for a camping trip with The Boys and loved it. They were able to sit inside with a table and lawn chairs to play poker while it was raining.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
10/12/2018 Update

Recently camped on the Oregon Coast and was notified of a storm warning. Packed my gear & firewood in the Core 6 and reinforced the stakes. It was noisy inside with all the wind so the dog and I ended up sleeping in the car. Winds hit 26 mph and the Core 6 took a pounding but stayed intact and functional. There was a little bit of puddling inside the next morning but that was on a side where the tent lifted and the footprint shifted out from under it and collected rain.
text_fidelity_b: CORE 6 Person Instant Cabin Tent | Portable Large Pop Up Tent with Easy 60 Second Camp Setup for Family Camping | Included Hanging Organizer for Outdoor Camping Accessories

text_fidelity_a: BYER OF MAINE, Pangean Glider Chair, Green, Now Partially Assembled, Perfect for Camping, Matching Furniture 38" D X 25" W X 39" H For starters I found this chair difficult to assemble.  The instructions looked like they'd taken a bad copy and reproduced it many times.  There was little definition of the diagrams.  It would've helped to be able to see the slots and bolt holes more clearly so you would know if you have the piece oriented correctly.  A couple of mistakes I made had to be corrected.  It took more than an hour to assemble what should've taken 15-20 minutes with instructions that were clear.  I found a You Tube that helped a bit though it had no sound and was in fast motion.  Another review mentioned arms would be nice, and I agree with that but it would be difficult to incorporate and not inline with the style of a sling chair.  So I subtracted a star for assembly difficulty. I also didn't find the chair to be all that comfortable, and because you stay in a reclining position it's not conducive to anything but laying back and relaxing.  Nothing wrong with relaxing, but having a cup of coffee or soda would be very clumsy unless you leaned forward to sip or drink.  And you would not be on eye level for conversation with others.  So I subtracted a star for this.  The quality however is very nice.  The wood is beautiful and once assembled it's very sturdy and you can tell it will last a long time.  I can see where others would give this 5 stars...particularly if they has someone assemble it for them and they found it to be more comfortable.  One more thing in closing...I considered this as a beach chair but a better application would be on a deck or by the pool.  It's not as light and convenient to carry as a conventional beach chair.
text_fidelity_b: BYER OF MAINE, Pangean Glider Chair, Green, Now Partially Assembled, Perfect for Camping, Matching Furniture 38" D X 25" W X 39" H

text_fidelity_a:
EXERPEUTIC EXERWORK 2000i Bluetooth Folding Exercise Desk Bike with 24 Workout Programs and Free App Ordered in October and it is now February. 4 months of use. Sort of.
The exercise-work-bike took a total of 3 days to put together, and had I been doing it alone, I probably never would have gotten it. There is some form of blue “insta-glue” on the pedal screws that made them nearly impossible to screw in. 3 neighborhood kids and teenagers tried their best to help a lady out, but to no avail. Eventually, I hung my head in shame and begged the assistance of male-friend to demonstrate his masculinity and wield tools to get the pedal screwed in.
I am 5’8. That’s 68 inches or about 172cm.
The next issue came when I realized that even at the lowest adjustment, the one recommended for 5’1-5’4 heights, I still struggled to reach the pedals, sitting with my back comfortably against the backrest. If I scooched forward just enough that half my cheeks were off the front of the seat I could reach the pedals, the backrest, and still use the desk for my laptop! But the desk was still a bit high, so I used the tilt-a-table adjustment to relax my wrists and type with perfectly non-ergonomical T-Rex arms.
And now the clunking noise. I can’t stand it. It started off quiet, but after maybe 100 miles of use, it makes a clunking noise from the pedals and no matter how many times I tighten the bolts (almost to stripping them), the seat keeps wobbling and the handle bars offer very little support.

Overall, as a workout bike, it give options that a regular bike doesn’t have—a table.
As for the rest, I am very unhappy with the very little use I got out of it, the lack of structural support for a solid working/workout of cycling, and how fast it has started having issues.
text_fidelity_b: EXERPEUTIC EXERWORK 2000i Bluetooth Folding Exercise Desk Bike with 24 Workout Programs and Free App

Empower Admittedly, it may seem too early for me to review the Empower Kettlebell & DVD I received yesterday. However, based on past workout purchases, and experiences, I believe this one's a keeper. I went for the 10-pound Kettlebell, and feel this is a good choice. It comes with a DVD with three levels of workouts, starting with one for beginners such as myself. It also includes warmup and cool-down routines, which are highly recommended before and after each workout respectively.

I started today, and after just one workout, I can already feel my core, leg, and arm muscles reacting to workout #1. While I have a little trouble with the 10-pound weight for some of the curl exercises, I modify the exercises to accommodate my lack of strength, and believe the 10-pound bell was a good choice because it allows me more room to grow -- which will be marked by my eliminating the need for modifications before moving on to the second workout.

In facing my 61st birthday, I'm active, and want to stay that way. This is why I'm determined to get in the best shape of my life (even in my early years, I've never been big on exercise). I started a month ago by purchasing a pair of Skecher Shape-ups, and taking brisk walks with my dogs each morning. To break the monotony, I purchased an MP3 player, and download books from the library. The time flies by!

I added resistance weeks ago with a trip to the gym, intent on going and working out every other day. Then reality hit. It took too long to get dressed, get my walk in, and then go to the gym, work out, come home and clean up. My mornings were shot. So I needed another way to achieve my goal.

A friend told me about Kettlebells. Now, after just one short Kettlebell workout, I've accomplished as much as when using several machines at the gym. The best part is it's fast. I can hop out of bed, and get it done quickly.

Based on numerous past workout experiences and money wasted on a variety of machines and other programs and gimmicks, I'm convinced this is what I've been searching for. I'd recommend it to anyone thinking of starting to get in shape, and wanting fast results. If you're new to working with weights, which I am not, you might want to start with the Empower 5-Pound KettleBell with DVD, and then work your way up to heavier Kettlebells. text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge 4 Special Edition Fitness and Activity Tracker with Built-in GPS, Heart Rate, Sleep & Swim Tracking, Black/Granite Reflective, One Size (S &L Bands Included) The fitbit as it comes out of the box (in late 2020) has lots of bugs. The settings function will lock it up if you try to use it. The weather app errors. It will not sync reliably. You would be thinking about returning it right now. But if you do some internet searches, you will find that these are known bugs that it leaves the factory with. If you install the mobile app, sync it and wait about 2 - 3 days the nyou will get the update that makes things work as they should. Do NOT uninstall the weather function of the fitbit just because it won't sync. If you do, it will no longer be available to re-install when device is updated. Just leave it there and wait for the update. Then weather and settings will work and syncing will become reliable.

It's absurd that fitbit would release such a defective product, but they do and they don't make any effort to tell you about the needed update.

After updating, it is quite a handy little tracker. The only fitbit tracker with a built in gps so you don't need to take your phone along. However be warned that your battery if fully charges will only last 4 - 5 hours when using the gps. It also takes a lot of time away from the standby time remaining.

Another feature they don't try to explain properly is the Spotify integration. Your fitbit can act as a very basic remote control for Spotify, but only if you subscribe to Spotify Premium. This means that to use the Spotify remote control feature you need 1) a paid Spotify subscription and 2) you need to have your phone with you. No music can be downloaded to the fitbit. It is just a simple play/stop/skip remote function for your phone and Spotify paid.

So those are all the things that fitbit doesn't want to tell you even after you buy it. After you get it updated, it is essentially a Charge 3 with built in battery sucking gps and paid Spotify remote control.

If you are new to fitbit and don't mind all the hassles getting it working right, it is a great little tracker. If you are thinking about upgrading from a fitbit Charge 3, the built in gps and Spotify remotes are the main differences.

Update: After all this it would never sync reliably. I would always have to reboot the device twice in a row to get sync started again. This hat do be done about every 36 hours.

Returned. Not worth it.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 4 Special Edition Fitness and Activity Tracker with Built-in GPS, Heart Rate, Sleep & Swim Tracking, Black/Granite Reflective, One Size (S &L Bands Included)

text_fidelity_a:
Topeak Explorer Rack I will first say the build quality of the rack seems good, and if you can get it mounted correctly to your specific bike, it will likely be a good rack for you.

However the rack could have been designed to fit more bikes better with a little more forethought. The product description says this rack is 16 x 14.5 x 9 inches. Maybe it is, however the critical dimension is the length of the support post for tire clearance reasons. The distance from the center of the bolt hole on the bottom, to the bent bar on top - ie the clearance measurement - is 14 and 15/16 inches. A 29er tire radius is obviously 14.5 inches, so if you were to mount the bottom of this level with your axle bolt you would have only 7/16 inch clearance - less than half an inch. Most rack mounting holes are well above the axle point, but some are not much. I was using P-clips since my frame has not rack holes, and even though I was completely free to mount wherever I wanted, I had trouble finding a usable position with much clearance. Since most 29ers are used in the mud at least on occasion, a little more clearance would have been nice.

Secondly, the hardware included is stainless M5 x 0.8, and there are just enough assuming your frame has the proper mounting holes. If your using P-clips or any other method, a trip to the hardware store will be required, and you likely won't find stainless hardware in metric. It wouldn't have killed them to add an extra bag of hardware for other bike mounting methods.

Lastly, if you plan to use the Topeak accessories for mounting then the top of the rack will be great for you. If your not, the top of the rack is not flat like most racks (because of the MTX grooves for easy accessory mounting). If your not using topeak bags and such, you should still be able to make it work fine, its just not flat.

Unfortunately there aren't many racks out there yet for 29ers, so this still might be a good fit for many.
text_fidelity_b: Topeak Explorer Rack

text_fidelity_a:
SteriPen Aqua UV Water Purifier The best type of drinking water purifier is a Steripen, in my opinion.

Filters: work well but you must keep them clean and sterile. This is hard to accomplish in a camp or when backpacking. I therefore rate that type last.

Chlorine tablets: These are slow. But the bottles are tiny a lipstick tube,so this is the most portable option. the tablets are protected and therefore always clean. No other system is as easy to keep the cleaning apparatus itself clean. Very effective. The big Con is that it puts a taste in the water. To me this is a small price to pay for all the other benefits. I rate this the best system for backpacking. And good enough for camping. But worst of all for emergency at home, especially long term emergency. Because slightly off tasting water is OK for 3 or 4 days, but who want to drink it for say three weeks? A missionary might have to drink poor tasting water for 3 or 4 years :(.

Steripen: The best all around system. I greatly prefer one that uses AA batteries instead of rechargeable. In emergencies or backpacking or camping long term: USB sources aren't necessarily going to be there. But penlight batteries last years until used and are very light and handy.

But it's not so foolproof as tablets because electronics can go wrong. But a teeny bottle holding 50 tablets has only one likely possibility of failing: the bottle is so tiny that you might lose it. Other than that: it is a foolproof system! But these tablets are dated: they do not last more than a couple years, they expire. So you have to buy more from time to time even if you aren't using them. But: they are very cheap!
text_fidelity_b: SteriPen Aqua UV Water Purifier

Where things get a bit more premium and specialized are the Kip Leather baseball gloves. These can be found in both USA Kip Leather and Japanese Kip Leather. Kip leather is usually the most preferred leather among professional players due to the light, firm, feel and higher quality of the leather. Kip leather comes from younger cattle, which creates a lighter hide that is extremely durable and taut, while also being a little bit easier to break in when compared to USA premium steerhide gloves.

Selecting Your Leather:

Cowhide Leather - Heavy leather, fastest break in time, medium quality, short durability, ideal for youth players.

Steerhide Leather - Heaviest leather, longest break in time, high quality, longest durability, ideal for high school and college players.

Kip Leather - Lighter leather, medium break in time, higher quality, long durability, ideal for college and pro players.

Japanese Kip Leather - Lightest leather, medium break in time, highest quality, long durability, ideal for elite pro players.

text_fidelity_a:
MOON LENCE Camping Chairs, Compact Backpacking Chair Small Folding Chair Lawn Chair with Side Pockets Portable Lightweight for Hiking & Beach & Fishing To begin with, I am 5’7” and 265lbs woman with majority of the weight distributed within my middle part, so most of the backpacking chairs are passing by without even looking my way. I wave “hi-by” to them all the time when I see them without any regret.
This one is great! It loved me from the moment we met :). Comfortable, durable, nice looking and omg!!! lightweight and compact when folded!!!
I don’t understand those, who complain that it’s hard to assemble or to pack it back together. C’mon y’all! Read my little guide, and I hope it will help you somewhat.
Take it out of the packing bag, just slightly wave it in your hand and everything jumps together making the frame almost ready to go! All the parts are connected with rubbery string inside the aluminum poles, so it makes it magically come together.
Than check each elbow to make sure that it sits well together, pressing slightly towards the corners.
Take fabric, unfold it with letters on the top, so you can read it. Put on one bottom corner first. Than pulling by the loop put on a second bottom corner. Than put one of the top corners next (right one for right-handed person and left one for left-handed person). The last corner will be a little harder to put on. To make it much quicker and easier, set the frame on the ground facing towards you. Put one foot on the horizontal lower part of the frame under the fabric to insure that frame will stay in place and won’t move when you don’t need it to move. While holding the frame firmly with your foot, pull the last loop upwards with your right hand while pulling the aluminum pole towards you and slightly pressing it down. You’ll see that this way it gets very easy and takes about 5-10 seconds to put the last corner on. I showed this to my 6th grader and he picked up the order of assembling quickly.
The process of packing it back it also very easy, once you pay attention to those little white drawings on the aluminum base. You take apart the poles and fold them. First do one upper side pole and hold it with your hand. While holding it, twist the base, so sides of it will come together. Now you’ll have all four sides of the base and one upper pole together in your hand. Hold it tightly and, using an other hand, keep pulling apart and folding an other pole adding it to your hand for holding. To fix shorter legs in place just pull them slightly towards the middle and press them
down with the longer ones. When everything put together, just wrap that velcro cord around and voila!!! This took me about a minute the most. My son did it himself without my help too. It took him about 5-7 minutes when he was doing it for the first time.
Put everything on one side of triple-folded fabric and roll. It will be tight enough and will easily fit inside that carrying bag leaving some space for the small universal anti-sinking sand mat (14.5”x14.5”) that you can get for about $14-15. Buy it!!! It will make whole lot of difference! Your chair will never sink into sand or any other soft surface! Believe me you won’t regret. It will add just about 2-4oz of extra weight, but it worth it. Should of being included with each chair already, but it’s the problem of every chair of this category.
Once again, I love this chair as well as my whole family. I went and ordered more of them.
text_fidelity_b: MOON LENCE Camping Chairs, Compact Backpacking Chair Small Folding Chair Lawn Chair with Side Pockets Portable Lightweight for Hiking & Beach & Fishing

Arachnid Cricket Pro 800 Standing Electronic Dartboard with Cherry Finish, Regulation 15.5” Target Area, 8-Player Score Display and 39 Games Brown I read every review on this item before ordering. There were some very good points that I needn't repeat in this review. I encourage anyone purchasing this dart board to read all the reviews to glean assembly hints.

The dart board came in one box and the box was a little beat up. None of the components were damaged though. Despite the outside condition of the box it was packaged well inside.

I read all the instructions before assembling. I utilized a small handle screw driver for assembly so I would be less likely to over tighten them and damage the press board. I did deviate from the instructions slightly. After assembling the main cabinet (the lower or base cabinet) I put the back on it while it was laying flat on the floor (be sure to line up the bottom of the back with the bottom of the bottom shelf, not the sides). This allowed me ensure that the cabinet was square before installing the door or the top. I installed the top section after standing up the cabinet.

Following the steps above should eliminate any door sag, or at least it did in my case. The completed unit is quite sound stable enough. However I did anchor it to the wall with a couple of L brackets at the top of the completed unit. I did not find it necessary to add any other brackets as others have indicated. We play on the board virtually every day and have had zero problems.

Why not 5 stars? The board has a function that allows you to play against the computer. It does not work on our board. Every thing else works, and it looks great. Best dart board I have ever had. I will be adding some lights in the canopy.
text_fidelity_b: Arachnid Cricket Pro 800 Standing Electronic Dartboard with Cherry Finish, Regulation 15.5” Target Area, 8-Player Score Display and 39 Games Brown

text_fidelity_a: ESEE Authentic Model 4HM Fixed Blade Knife, Black Powder Blade, Micarta Handle, Leather Sheath I have experience with 4X ESEE knives, and there is a tool for every job - I love them all.  I bought this one to "downsize" from the ESEE Laser Strike which I found to be way too heavy to carry all day, and while a phenomenal knife, was not as well suited for smaller tasks.  This one I found to be the perfect size for just about everything you do in the outdoors.  Also, for folks with smaller hands, or a desire to work the blade more deftly, the smaller handle drops weight and is more easy to manipulate vs. it's larger cousins. After much experimentation, I've settled on carrying this knife as well as the tiny fisherman version which has a very small blade (2.5 inch) and is perfect for squirrel and fish work.  The two together cover most tasks well.  I also purchased an aftermarket fire steel with a kydex sheath which I added later. I then had to MOD the blade by ever-so-gently using an electric wire brush to remove just about an inch of the blade coating on the spine of the blade right near the handle so you can effectively spark the fire steel.  Now, that will require extra oil maintenance to prevent rust, but if you take care of your tools, they will take care of you.  I would love to see ESEE create a sheath which could house all three items (anybody listening?).  Now if you are bushcrafting, remember to always carry a folding saw (safer) or a small axe.  With those four tools, and a sharpening stone, you can rebuild civilization!  If you have never had an ESEE knife, you will love this, so don't hesitate as it is bomb proof and will last you forever.  If you could only have one blade and your life depended on it, this is the one.  I may make some videos on this knife and when I do, you can find them at "Thecameracommando" on youtube.  Cheers and happy camping!
text_fidelity_b: ESEE Authentic Model 4HM Fixed Blade Knife, Black Powder Blade, Micarta Handle, Leather Sheath

Counted: 40, as advertised.
Rattle effect: out of the bag, they all rattle.
Putting them to the test, time will tell.

These little rattles look to be the perfect size. Smaller than they appear in the photo in the listing, which is great. I didn't want rattles the size of ping pong balls.
These are a bit smaller than the average marble.

After finally using the rattles for a day of fishing, here's a bit of an addendum:

Using four of the rattles, when I reeled in to pack in to go home, the "chrome on all four was totally gone. They were all four totally white.
For me, this is no problem. The fish don't care if they're chrome or white.
Something else that I wondered about, with no mention in any of the reviews... the rattle effect is created by one bb sized steel ball inside each side of each rattle. (To give an idea on size of the rattles, only one bb size steel ball will fit in each side.)

The rattle effect is quite audible.

text_fidelity_a: Tenzing TZ 720 Lumbar Pack (AP Camo) Let me start by saying that I researched literally dozens of fanny packs before settling on this one. Badlands,Fieldline, LL Bean, ALPS, Allen, Timberhawk, Browning, Cabelas .  .  . you get the picture. I use a fanny pack primarily to run and gun longbeards and to get my archery gear into my hunting locations with a Summit Open Shot Climber on my back. This pack replaces an old fleece 380 cubic inch Fieldline that served me well for many years, but was always just a tad too small.  I can tell you that there are a limited number of packs available that are between what I consider to be too small at 450-500 cubic inches, and for me, too large at over 1000 cubic inches. I don't carry enough gear to require backpack type straps, nor do I want the complications associated with them. Furthermore, many  of the packs that DO tend to fall inside this capacity range  have what I call a "hopper" style zippered opening, which to me makes absolutely no sense. You unzip it and your gear rolls out. I want a top loading pack that retains my gear. If I've just climbed 20' , gotten settled in, unzip my pack and all my gear falls to the ground, well, lets just say I'm not a happy camper. This is a nicely designed pack that met the majority of my parameters developed over 40 years of hunting. This pack, in my opinion, is the perfect size. Enough room for all my gadgets and grub. The side straps "fold" easily and stay "folded" for  easy placement at the back of my platform. Lashing straps top and bottom, check. Plenty of zippered organizing compartments, check. Side strap pockets that actually have some capacity, check.  Oh. . Did I mention this is a great looking pack?  Which leads us to one of my few negatives. The attractive green panels that you see on the front and top of the pack as well as  the entire pack bottom are Dyneema, a super strong synthetic fiber material. Noisy??  Not terribly. Tenzing claims these panels are used for durability, and while I'm fairly certain this pack will indeed outlive my remaining years in the field, they are . . well . . synthetic.  While in my application it means little, if I were using this pack primarily  to stalk or still hunt, it might impact my choice. Get one in your hands and see for yourself. Sizing issue: The reviewer that  mentioned this not cinching up to his 34 waist is spot on. The side straps, at least on the pack i was shipped, are simply too long. I am a 35 waist and can JUST get this pack tight enough. Overall I am extremely happy with the design, build quality, and my Amazon purchase. Nicely done Tenzing.
text_fidelity_b: Tenzing TZ 720 Lumbar Pack (AP Camo)

text_fidelity_a:
Moxi Skates - Beach Bunny - Fashionable Womens Roller Skates Color: Watermelon. Skate Size: 7 (My normal shoe/boot size is 8-8.5 in US womens)
First, they are soooo cute! I love the color combo. I'm 50 yrs old and decided to get back into roller skating. I used to do this casually when I was in my teens, but was never exceptional at it. I thought this would be a fun way to get some more exercise in my life. So far its working! You engage so many muscles when roller skating. It takes balance, core and leg strength to keep from falling on your bum. These are made of vinyl so they are quite stiff at first and take some time break in. My hubby purchased these as a gift. He purchased according to the size chart and they fit well/snug with a thick sock. I normally wear a size 8 in U.S women’s shoes. When it comes to boots I typically buy 8.5 (to allow for thicker sock). Hubby purchased the size 7 skates as the chart indicated. This was just right. I thought they might be a bit tight at first. But with use, I realized the size was perfect. You want your foot to be held firmly as you will be moving around a lot. I imagine if they were looser, my foot would flex more and potentially cause strain in the foot muscles so I think the snug sizing is perfect. Measure your foot and look at size chart and you should be fine. I like that the skates have a metal base plate instead of plastic. This feels sturdier/safer. The wheels roll well on blacktop streets (even better on my hardwood floors inside my house). There are a couple things that were a bit odd. First the vinyl is so thick its a bit uncomfortable (specifically around the ankle) until they get worn in. And it takes a while to wear them in.
Second, the laces on one skate were a whole foot longer than the laces on the other skate. This trips out my OCD brain. I will have to replace them.

Overall, I think these are good skates for beginners (of all ages). They are made well and of good quality. Just be patient with the wear in period.
text_fidelity_b: Moxi Skates - Beach Bunny - Fashionable Womens Roller Skates

So be careful with the 2 short bars as you can have them positioned incorrectly. Also the bar is very uncomfortable to try and do seated dips on. There just isn't a great place for your hands to sit comfortably but that's about the only exercise out of the many it is designed for that isn't perfect. I'd recommend this bar to anyone trying to avoid a gym membership but still wants to maintain strength.

I usually wake up a million times during the night when camping. This time I only woke up once, and that was because of an earthquake!

This sleeping bag's material has a soft, dry feel to it; not at all sweaty and swampy. It works best, counter-intuitively, when you don't sleep with tons of layers on. I just wear my undies. If you're too cold, you're best off adding your coat and your other layers on top of your sleeping bag, not inside of it.

I'm not sure why I bought the 32 degree bag when much of my camping is done well below that... I also do some warmer trips so I'll probably keep this and also buy the heavier one, too.

I also have the Ibera waterproof panniers. I wish this was as waterproof as those panniers. I also wish it mounted better to the Ibera brand bike rack. It mounts "ok" but it's not as great as you would expect for a product that is made to work together. The clip mechanism is relatively easy to use to release the bike but it's fickle sometimes; often requiring quite a bit of effort to get clipped on or release. It feels like the clip mechanism does not move very freely and gets jammed with dirty easily. I strongly recommend getting the rain cover if you plan on using this in the rain without any other bags to put stuff in when the rain starts. I've been stuck in the rain a few times and the first time I didn't realize how porous the material of this bag was and my stuff got damp. Now, if I am expecting rain, I put my phone, hat and other things I want to keep dry in the waterproof pannier instead of the trunk bag.

Overall, this bag is great for light, dry weather commuter use. The removable shoulder strap is a nice touch. If you plan to ride in the rain either buy the rain cover, buy a different trunk or put your stuff in a waterproof bag.
text_fidelity_b: Ibera 2 in 1 PakRak Commuter Bicycle Trunk Bag with Expandable Panniers, Clip On Quick Release Design and Detachable Shoulder Strap
